data.summary: The pod startup was delayed primarily by the model download process, which accounted for 25.6 seconds of the total 33.0-second startup time. The model weights were fetched from a remote source on every startup because the cache hit attribute was false. Other potential bottlenecks, such as CPU throttling, were found to be negligible.

findings.statement: The model.download span took 25.648 seconds, representing the majority of the 33.0-second total startup time.
The model download cache_hit attribute was false, confirming that 262,144,000 bytes were re-downloaded from the remote model hub during this startup.
CPU throttling was negligible with a mean ratio of 0.017, indicating that application initialisation was not constrained by CPU limits.

ruled_out.reason: CPU throttling metrics show a very low mean of 0.017, ruling out CPU-bound performance issues during initialisation.
The image pull duration was 4.921 seconds, which is significantly lower than the 25.648 seconds spent on model downloading.

recommendations.rationale: Implementing a persistent volume for model weights ensures they persist across pod restarts, avoiding the need to re-download them from the remote store.
Enabling the application's native cache reuse mechanism will allow it to detect existing weights on disk, preventing redundant downloads.
Using a prefetch job ensures that weights are available locally before the application starts, reducing the impact of the initial download.
